ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure is a transition-state structure, with the main body being a left-right fused bicyclic system; the left side is a six-membered ring and bears a left-side carbonyl O; the right side is a five-membered ring and bears a carbonyl O at the upper right. The two rings share a middle bridgehead-bridgehead bond. The upper bridgehead has an upward wedge substituent bond, and the lower bridgehead is connected to OH. The figure also has curved arrows, B:, H, and O-H/C-H related labels, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows and excluding bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning count: the left six-membered ring skeleton counts as 6 heavy-atom bonds, including the middle shared bridgehead-bridgehead bond. The left carbonyl C=O counts as 1 bond. The right five-membered ring only adds bonds not already counted in the left ring: upper bridgehead to carbonyl carbon, carbonyl carbon to right ring carbon, right ring carbon to lower ring carbon, lower ring carbon to lower bridgehead, and the right carbonyl C=O, for a total of 5 bonds. Then add 1 upward wedge substituent bond from the upper bridgehead, and 1 bond from the lower bridgehead to the O in OH; O-H or C-H is not counted. The total is 6 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 1 = 14.
